claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic NbMoTaW.
As-cast equiatomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Untreated NbMoTaW has good high-temperature strength through approximately 1600 °C.
Untreated, as-cast equiatomic NbMoTaW has poor room-temperature ductility.
The high-dose helium-irradiation behavior of NbMoTaW has not been experimentally verified.
Warm forging at approximately 1200 °C followed by annealing at 1000–1200 °C will refine the grain substructure of NbMoTaW.
The proposed processing will stabilize a single-phase BCC substructure in NbMoTaW.
Warm forging will introduce a high density of dislocation networks in NbMoTaW.
Warm forging will introduce subgrain boundaries in NbMoTaW.
The dislocation networks and subgrain boundaries will act as irradiation-defect sinks and reduce irradiation damage.
Sub-solvus annealing at 1000–1200 °C will stabilize the forged interfaces.
Stabilization of the forged interfaces will preserve the BCC phase at elevated temperatures.
The proposed processing will reduce low-temperature brittleness.
The processed alloy will have at least 10–20% higher room-temperature plastic strain before fracture than untreated NbMoTaW.
Following helium irradiation, the processed alloy will contain fewer and smaller helium-induced bubbles than untreated NbMoTaW.
The processed alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to untreated NbMoTaW over 1000–1600 °C.
The proposed treatment will be effective under helium-ion irradiation at approximately 300–800 °C.
The processed material will retain a structurally stable BCC phase up to approximately 1600 °C.
Annealing may cause unwanted phase precipitation or grain growth that counteracts the intended improvements.
The treatment's phase stability above 10^23 ions/m² and its response to high-dose neutron irradiation remain unvalidated.
